messages:
cust-492: Hey team — after the pinned model upgrade on our account, our embeddings responses switched from 1024 -> 1536 dims. We pinned via the dashboard to the alias 'embed-base:stable'. Sample response attached.

maria: Sorry — can you paste the request_id and the model name/version that shows up in the response (or any response headers)? Also which workspace/team id?

cust-492: request_id: req_0a1b2c3d, team_id: team_cust492
curl example we used:
```
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-base:stable","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```
Response excerpt: `{ "model": "embed-base", "data": [{ "embedding": [ ... ] }], "meta": { "embedding_length": 1536 } }`

alex: Two likely causes: 1) alias pin -> alias can fallback to a different variant if exact version not available 2) batchpad/routing could route to a different capacity-backed variant (e.g., embed-large-v2) which has 1536 dims. Can you check if the dashboard shows a "variant fallback" on your pinned alias?

cust-492: Dashboard shows pinned to 'embed-base:stable' (no explicit sha). We didn't expect alias to switch.

observability-bot: :rotating_light: Fallback rule triggered for team_cust492 at 1725987700 — routed requests to model: embed-large-v2 (variant dims=1536) due to capacity shortage on embed-base@2026-03-15.

devon: Confirmed — our routing logs show a fallback for your requests between 1725987689-1725987760. The alias 'embed-base:stable' was resolved to a different variant because the pinned alias pointed at an alias group without an immutable version. That allowed runtime to substitute embed-large-v2 when embed-base capacity was saturated.

maria: Short-term fixes:
- Pin to an immutable version ID: e.g. `embed-base@sha256:abcd1234` (dashboard -> model -> versions -> copy version id) OR
- Set `X-AllowVariantFallback: false` header in your requests to prevent runtime fallbacks.

Example: get model versions
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/embed-base/versions
```
Pin via API (example)
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"team_id":"team_cust492","pin":"embed-base@sha256:abcd1234","allow_fallback":false}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/teams/pins
```

alex: Also check response header `x-model-version` — that tells you the exact version used. If it equals a different model id (embed-large-v2) that's the problem.

devon: We've applied a temporary mitigation: pinned team_cust492 to embed-base@sha256:abcd1234 and set allow_fallback=false for the account. We'll monitor.

cust-492: Re-ran tests — embeddings are back to 1024 dims. Verified `x-model-version: embed-base@sha256:abcd1234` in response. Thanks!

maria: Great. We'll follow up with the infra team to improve alias safety and clearer dashboard warnings on "alias pins" vs immutable pins. Marking this thread resolved. :thumbsup:
